evidence.basis: attempt to use remainder theorem (M1); 2-q+r=12 A1; r-q=10; EITHER sum and product of roots (A1); attempt to use identity (M1); equation (A1); attempt to solve simultaneous equations (M1); THEN q=-7, r=3 A1

blocks.task_summary: Prove by contradiction that sqrt(xy) ≤ (x+y)/2 for all x, y ∈ ℝ⁺.

Simplify to 0 > x^2 - 2xy + y^2
Rewrite as 0 > (x - y)^2
Conclude contradiction since square is non-negative

evidence.basis: M1: assume sqrt(xy) > (x+y)/2; M1: attempt to square both sides; A1: 0 > x^2 - 4xy + y^2 OR 0 > y^2 - 4xy + x^2; A1: 0 > (x - y)^2 OR 0 > (y - x)^2; R1: a square number can never be negative hence contradiction
